The accounting period a filing declares

Source: R/period.R
xbrl_period.Rd

A filing states its own reporting period as facts, and the preceding one alongside it. Reading them beats inferring the period from the contexts: the contexts hold whatever periods the filer happened to tag, comparatives and note periods included, so the latest is not reliably the accounting year and the earliest is not reliably its start.

Usage

xbrl_period(x)

Arguments

x

A tibble from read_xbrl().

Value

A one-row tibble with start, end, prev_start and prev_end as Date. A field the filing does not declare is NA. Where a filing states a date more than once, the first is taken.

The taxonomy's typo

The preceding period's end is PredingReportingPeriodEndDate – not Preceding, which is how its own start date is spelled two elements earlier. The misspelling is in the published taxonomy, so it is what filings carry and what this looks for. Both spellings are accepted, because a filer who corrects it should not be punished for it.

How often it is there

Across 4,304 Danish filings from 2020-2024 every one declared its current period, and 3,950 declared the preceding one – a filing states both dates of a period or neither. So this is a reliable route rather than a lucky one – but NA still comes back where a filing is silent, and callers should have a fallback rather than assume.

See also

read_xbrl(), and check_movement(), which uses this to pair an opening balance with the year its movements cover.

Other taxonomy: add_taxonomy(), check_breakdown(), check_cascade(), check_cashflow(), check_continuity(), check_inclusion(), check_movement(), check_statement(), read_taxonomy(), xbrl_accounts(), xbrl_company(), xbrl_fill(), xbrl_lines(), xbrl_movements(), xbrl_note_tables(), xbrl_panel(), xbrl_ratios(), xbrl_report(), xbrl_report_data(), xbrl_resolve(), xbrl_robustness(), xbrl_screen(), xbrl_standardise(), xbrl_validate()

Examples

if (FALSE) { # \dontrun{
x <- read_xbrl("filing.xml")
p <- xbrl_period(x)

# the opening balance of the year is the closing balance of the one before
p$prev_end
} # }
